assessment: Edgar mints a Vampire on every Vampire cast; the deck's job is to make that entry hurt three seats at once. The measurement says the multiplier half is finished and the payoff half is not, so three of the ten are entry-trigger payoffs and none is a doubler. The bench is twenty-nine entries and it is a box of small Vampires: two of them duplicate cards already in the 99, one is outside the colour identity, and most of the rest convert Blood tokens or eat a creature. Three bench cards clear the bar on their own terms — Vampire Nocturnus, Akroma's Memorial and Markov Baron — and the tail loses its slots to the pool because nothing in the box converts a creature entry into damage, answers a two-mana permanent, or produces a black source. The floor is 4 before and after every one of the ten.

ten.closes: engine component: the entry-trigger payoff class (Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight — 52.5% assembled, 25.8% of opening sevens)
ten.why: Its trigger is word-for-word the one stack 009 resolved — whenever another creature you control enters, deal 1 damage to each opponent — and 009 is checker-passed that an ability triggers once per occurrence, so a doubled eminence token on a two-mana Vampire pays it twice, not once. Four payoffs is 25.8% of an opening seven and five is 31%; this is the single cheapest way to buy that step, at {2}{R} in the colour the base over-serves (17 red sources for eleven cards that each want one red pip).
ten.unlocks: A fifth copy of the deck's primary kill condition, so the turn-three Cordial Vampire line from stack 009 stops needing Purphoros specifically.

ten.closes: engine component: THE GO-WIDE KILL — a token-to-damage payoff AND a multiplier (40.2% assembled, 27.5% by turn six)
ten.why: Three tokens per combat in a four-player pod, tapped and attacking, is three creature-entry events every turn you attack — the event Impact Tremors, Purphoros, Corpse Knight and Warleader's Call all read, and the event Cathars' Crusade turns into a counter on every creature you control. This is not a ninth doubler: it raises the number of entries the four payoffs see rather than multiplying one of them, so it works on the 47.5% of boards where no payoff has shown up yet by giving Edgar's tokens a body count to hide behind.
ten.unlocks: A repeating token source on the attack step, which is the one timing the deck's eight multipliers do not cover.

ten.closes: engine component: the noncreature answer (Despark, Anguished Unmaking — two cards, 30.8% assembled, 13.7% of opening sevens)
ten.why: Anguished Unmaking is the deck's only answer to a cheap noncreature permanent: Despark exiles mana value 4 or greater, and Ghostly Prison and Propaganda are 3, Rest in Peace and Torpor Orb 2. Against a Torpor Orb the whole payoff class is blanked at once, so the answer slot is what restores the primary kill; Generous Gift destroys any permanent at instant speed for {2}{W} and doubles that class from one card to two.
ten.unlocks: An answer to a two-mana artifact or enchantment, which nothing in the 99 currently has.

combo_lines_opened.produces: whether a doubled token-creation event drains once or twice

ten.closes: engine component: the entry-trigger payoff class (Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight — 52.5% assembled)
ten.why: A sixth converter that reads token creation rather than creature entry, on a 2/3 flier for {3}{B}, so it drains three seats off Legion's Landing, Bloodline Keeper's tap and Charismatic Conqueror's punish as well as off eminence. It ranks below Witty Roastmaster because its wording is not the one stack 009 verified: whether Anointed Procession's doubled creation gives it one trigger or two is an open question and it should be sleeved on the base rate, not on the doubled one.
ten.unlocks: Each-opponent drain from token-making that does not go through a creature spell, and a flying body the ground stall cannot block.

ten.closes: engine component: the combat kill (nine lords and anthems, 83.2% assembled) — the fallback the verdict prices as a losing plan into ~120 combined life
ten.why: The best card in the box by a distance: every eminence token is a Vampire, so a live Nocturnus turns a board of 1/1s into a board of 3/2 fliers and the combat plan stops caring about three walls of ground blockers. The honest price is the mana — {1}{B}{B}{B} against 26 black sources where Karsten asks 33 for that cost — so it is a turn-five card in practice, and its anthem is conditional on the top card of your library being black.
ten.when: Sleeve it when the pod is playing ground creatures and the games are ending in a stall rather than to a trigger; it is the bench's answer to boards you cannot get through.

ten.closes: card-advantage (axis reads 3 against a target of 10)
ten.why: Read the axis with its own probe before spending slots on it: deck-audit names eight more cards showing the function — Castle Locthwain, Henrika Domnathi, Midgar, Minas Tirith, Preacher of the Schism, Savai Triome, Silent Clearing and Sunbaked Canyon — and Caretaker's Talent plus Welcoming Vampire already convert a token wave into cards, so the count is a floor and 3-against-10 overstates it. What the deck genuinely has none of is a source that pays the turn after a wrath, when Caretaker's Talent and Welcoming Vampire both read zero; this draws every upkeep for three mana and never touches a graveyard. One such pick, not two — a second would be answering a question rather than a hole.
ten.unlocks: Draw that is live on an empty board, which is the turn the sweeper math says initiative is decided on.

cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
combo_lines_opened.produces: one opponent loses life equal to the Vampire count twice over

ten.closes: engine component: the entry-trigger payoff class (Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight) — deck-audit names it a closer for this component
ten.why: It is a Vampire, so casting it mints a token before its own entry resolves and that token counts toward X: on the turn-six board the simulation measures at 4.1 bodies it drains every seat for five or more and gains you the same. Protection from white is the second half of the pick — it walks past Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Winds of Abandon and a white blocker, which is what a five-mana finisher has to survive to matter.
ten.unlocks: A one-shot each-opponent drain sized by width, and a lifegain event large enough that Vito's redirect is worth reading as a kill rather than a trickle.

ten.closes: colour-sources (black reads 26 against a 36 target, the worst colour at −10)
ten.why: Black carries the deck's heaviest costs — Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Twilight Prophet, Sanctum Seeker and Bloodline Keeper all want two black pips — on 26 sources, while red gets 17 sources for eleven cards that never ask for more than one red pip. A pathway played on its Grimclimb face is an untapped black source in a slot that currently pays a life for red-or-white; call it one source, because the 36-source yardstick assumes 40 lands and a 37-land three-colour base cannot reach it.
ten.unlocks: An untapped black source with no life cost, in an aggro base already carrying three unconditional taplands.

ten.closes: engine component: the combat kill (nine lords and anthems, 83.2% assembled) — the fallback the verdict prices as a losing plan
ten.why: The box's one haymaker: flying, first strike, vigilance, trample and haste to a board of tokens ends a stalled game on the turn it resolves, and it is colourless so it costs the mana base nothing. Seven mana against 5.3 mean available mana at turn six is the whole argument against it — it is the card you want in the games the trigger plan did not close, not the card you want in the games it did.
ten.when: Sleeve it against pods that go long and defend on the ground; leave it in the box against fast tables, where a seven-drop is a mulligan you kept.

ten.closes: engine component: the combat kill (nine lords and anthems, 83.2% assembled)
ten.why: Convoke is what earns it the last slot: on the wide board this deck is built to have, a third lord costs {B} or nothing, and casting a Vampire is itself an eminence trigger, so the anthem arrives with a body attached. It is ranked tenth honestly — the lord component is the deck's most reliable at 83.2% and a tenth anthem is the lowest-leverage add on this list.
ten.when: Sleeve it when the curve feels heavy and you want a three-drop that is free on a developed board; skip it if the payoff class is what you are short of.

gaps: No obsolescence claim is made. The index's 21 hits for this deck read Aerith Gainsborough and Syr Vondam as replacements for Elenda, Scrapwork Mutt and Fear of Missing Out for Cemetery Gatekeeper, and Hoofprints of the Stag for Caretaker's Talent; read the oracle text and none of them makes a Vampire, converts an entry into damage, or answers a permanent. None of the ten appears in the index as a replacement for anything in the 99.

No synergy claim is made either. All 25 pool candidates are Auras sharing the identical five 'Aura + Protection' partners — one rule firing on a type line, not a lead — and nine of the ten picks have no in-deck partner on their own shortlist at all. The tenth, Brightclimb Pathway, lists Herald's Horn, which is a cost-reduction artifact of the same rule set.

Mirkwood Bats' interaction with the doublers is unsettled. Stack 009 established that an ability reading 'whenever another creature you control enters' triggers once per occurrence, so Anointed Procession's second token pays it twice; Mirkwood Bats reads 'whenever you create or sacrifice a token', and whether one doubled creation event is one drain or two is a different question. A resolve-stack run would settle it, and the pick is ranked on the single-trigger reading.

Akroma's Memorial's protection from black and from red is not claimed as a sweeper answer. Protection stops damage, so it plausibly blanks a red damage-based wipe, but Toxic Deluge is -X/-X and Wrath of God destroys — neither is prevented. Which wipes it actually answers is a rules question no stack in this deck has asked.

Three of the ten are castability stretches and mana-analysis has not been re-run for them. Against Karsten, Adeline's {1}{W}{W} wants 29 sources and the base has 21, Phyrexian Arena's {1}{B}{B} wants 29 against 26, and Vampire Nocturnus's {1}{B}{B}{B} wants 33 against 26. All three are still castable a turn late; none is a turn-three play as often as its mana value suggests.

Five of the ten carry no natural_cut, deliberately. Five cuts are all this list can defend — Kalitas, Olivia's Wrath, Swiftfoot Boots, Sanguine Bond and Sunbaked Canyon — and two of those are priced rather than free: cutting Sanguine Bond takes the deck from two verified two-card infinites to one and strands stack 006, and cutting Olivia's Wrath takes the one-sided wipe out of a deck that will hold more non-Vampires than it does now. Toxic Deluge is the other sweeper and stays.

The card-advantage axis cannot be settled from the count. It reads 3 against a target of 10, but deck-audit's own probe names eight cards the taxonomy filed elsewhere and the draw-engine component measures 60.3% assembled. Only one draw pick is taken here; whether the deck wants a second is a question a goldfish re-run after Phyrexian Arena lands would answer better than any card list.

The bench's EDHREC ranks are absent from sideboard-facts for all 29 entries while cards.csv carries one for each (Vampire Nocturnus 8795, Markov Baron 3552, Akroma's Memorial 1219). The ranks quoted here come from cards.csv, and none of the three bench picks was chosen on popularity — sideboard-facts is right that the argument has to rest on the deck's own needs.
